lines.text: מושׁ 550 מות
* I. מוּשׁ 1. to give way, to recede,
to depart; absol. Is. 22, 25. 54, 10;
with acc. of place whither, Zech. 14, 4;
מִן of place whence, Num. 14, 44. Judg.
54, 10; מִלִּפְנֵי of pers. Jer. 31, 36.—Not
found in the kindred dialects.
2. Causat. to put away, to remove,
Zech. 3, 9.
Hiph. 1. Trans. to let remove, to let
go, e. g. prey, Nah. 3, 1; to withdraw
from, c. מִן, Mic. 2, 3 from which ye
shall not withdraw your necks. v. 4.
2. More frequently i. q. Kal, to give
way, to withdraw, to depart, absol. Ex.
13, 22. Job 23, 12; with מִן of place, Ex.
מִן c. inf. Jer. 17, 8 וְלֹא יָמִישׁ מֵעֲשׂוֹת פֶּרִי
and doth not withdraw (cease) from
yielding fruit.
* II. מוּשׁ i. q. מָשַׁשׁ and יָמַשׁ, to feel,
to touch, to try by the touch, Gen. 27, 21.
Hiph. id. Ps. 115, 7. Judg. 16, 26
Keri.
Deriv. pr. n. מוּשִׁי.
מוֹשָׁב m. (r. יָשַׁב) constr. מוֹשַׁב, c. suff.
מוֹשָׁבִי; plur. constr. מוֹשְׁבוֹת, once מוֹשְׁבֵי
7. Of things, as a city, seat, i. e. site,
situation, 2 K. 2, 19.
2. a sitting, session, an assembly of
persons sitting together, Ps. 1, 1. 107,
3. seat, dwelling, Gen. 27, 39. Num.
a dwelling-house, Lev. 25, 19. עִיר מוֹשָׁב
a city of dwelling, to dwell in, Ps. 107, 4.
7. Meton. a time of abode, Ex. 12, 40.
Concr. dwellers, inhabitants, 2 Sam. 9,
12 כֹּל־מוֹשַׁב בֵּית צִיבָא.
מוּשִׁי (prob. for מוּשִׁיָּה felt out by Je-
hovah, r. מוּשׁ II) Mushi, pr. n. m. Ex. 6,
19. Num. 3, 20; defect. מֻשִׁי 1 Chr. 6, 4.
—Patronym. also מוּשִׁי for מוּשִׁיִי Num.
מוֹשְׁכוֹת f. plur. (r. מָשַׁךְ) the drawers,
poet. for cords, bands, with which one is
bound, Job 38, 31. Comp. Arab. مَسَكَةٌ
a fetter, from مسك firmiter tenuit.
מוֹשָׁעוֹת f. plur. (r. יָשַׁע) deliverances,
* מוּת præt. מֵת, מַתִּי, plur. מֵתוּ,
מַתְנוּ; inf. abs. מוֹת, constr. מוּת; imper.
מֻת; fut. יָמוּת, 3 pers. תָּמֹת, conv. וַיָּמָת.
1. to die, and so in all the Semitic lan-
guages; Arab. مات mid. Waw, Syr.
ܡܺܝܬ. The middle radical ו, however,
seems to be softened down from the liquid
ר, comp. דָּרַשׁ, דּוּשׁ; so that the primary
root is probably mrt, comp. Sanscr. mri
to die, mrita dead, mrityu death, also
mâth, muth, mith, mêth, mid, mêd, to
kill; Malay mita to kill and to die; Zend.
mreté, mereté, Pehlv. murdéh, mard, mor-
tal, man; Pers. مردن to die, Gr. μορ-
τός i. q. βροτός, Lat. mors, mortis, Morta
in Liv. Andr. Germ. Mord, in old Germ.
used not only of killing but also for death,
Engl. murder.—Spoken of the death of
men or animals, Ex. 11, 5. Ecc. 9, 4;
both natural Gen. 5, 8. 11. 14. 17. 20. 27.
31. al. sæpiss. and violent Ex. 21, 12.
1, 19. al. The instrument or cause of
death is put usually with בְּ, Num. 35, 17.
19. al. Josh. 10, 11 more died בְּאַבְנֵי הַבָּרָד
of the hail-stones than, etc. Judg. 15, 18
אָמוּת בַּצָּמָא I die of thirst. Ez. 5, 12;
also מִפְּנֵי Jer. 38, 9.—Freq. is the phrase
מוֹת יָמוּת dying he shall die, i. e. he shall
surely die, Gen. 2, 17. 3, 4. 20, 7. 1 Sam.
14, 39. 44. 2 Sam. 12, 14. al. Slightly
different is the phrase מוֹת יוּמָת with fut.
Hoph. he shall surely be put to death,
used in the Mosaic law to denote punish-
חָלָה לָמוּת to be sick unto death, 2 K. 20,
1. 2 Chr. 32, 24; and hyperbol. Judg. 16,
16 קָצְרָה נַפְשׁוֹ לָמוּת his soul was vexed
unto death, impatient.—Trop. the heart
of any one is said to die, i. e. to faint, to
fail, 1 Sam. 25, 37; comp. opp. חָיָה
Gen. 45, 27. Judg. 15, 19. So the trunk
of a tree Job 14, 8, comp. הָרַג; or land
untilled, Gen. 47, 19 why should we die,
we and our land, which is afterwards
explained by וְהָאֲדָמָה לֹא תֵשָׁם. Comp.
Arab. مات inculta, sterilis, deserta fuit
63.—Spoken ironically Job 12, 2 עִמָּכֶם
תָּמוּת חָכְמָה wisdom will die with you.—

line_status.note: The line begins with a printed מִן (hireq under mem, final nun) at the far left before "c. inf."; Reading A omits it. The Hebrew citation is otherwise identical in both readings and matches the print (וְלֹא, יָמִישׁ, מֵעֲשׂוֹת with sin dot, פֶּרִי with dagesh and segol).

The kaf carries a dot printed above it (holem) and a dagesh inside, with no qamets beneath — so כֹּל, not כָּל. All other points (שׁ shin dot, holem-vav, patah, tsere, hiriq, qamets) match both readings.

The decisive difference is the dagesh in the yod of the second word: the image shows a dot printed inside the yod of מוּשִׁיָּה (yod with dagesh + qamets), so Reading B is correct; Reading A omits it. All other characters, vowels, shureq and shin dots agree in both readings and match the print.

The headword is printed plene: a distinct vav stroke stands between the mem and the shin, carrying the holem (six letters מ-ו-ש-כ-ו-ת), so Reading A's מוֹשְׁכוֹת is correct and B's defective מֹשְׁכוֹת is not what is printed. The rest of the line is identical in both readings and matches the image.
The final tāʾ marbūṭa carries a clearly printed tanwīn (dammatan, the small hooked mark above the ة); Reading A omits it. Fatḥas on م, س, ك as in both readings.

Decisive point is the vowel on the constr. form: in the inf. abs. the dot sits clearly above the vav (holem, מוֹת), whereas in the constr. form the dot sits lower, at the left of the vav's shaft (shureq, מוּת). Reading B matches the print; A wrongly repeats holem.
Final word is printed וַיָּמָת with qamets under the mem; there is no holem dot above the mem (contrast the visible holem dot on תָּמֹת just before it).
Printed order after "comp." is דָּרַשׁ first (left), then דּוּשׁ (right, before the semicolon); Reading A reverses the two items. Vowel points, dagesh and shin dots on both words are as in Reading B.

Under the mem of יוּמָת the printed vowel has a small vertical stem below the horizontal bar — a qamets, not a flat patach. Reading B is correct (standard Hophal יוּמָת); everything else in the line is identical in both readings.

Under the shin of תֵשָׁם the print shows a qamets (T-shaped, with a tail), not a flat patach, and there is no dagesh in the shin — only the shin dot above; this matches Gen. 47:19 niphal תֵשָׁם. Reading B's patach + dagesh is wrong.
Under the mem the print shows a qamets (T-shaped bar with a stem), not a shewa (two vertical dots); the dagesh in mem is also printed. Reading A matches.
